prompt: Add a Node.js backend route that searches for podcast episodes about a user-provided topic.
context: Node.js API server using native fetch

invariants: Read LISTEN_API_KEY only on the server
Send X-ListenAPI-Key to the production API
Encode the user query with URLSearchParams or an equivalent structured API
Handle non-2xx responses without exposing the key
Do not add an SDK when native fetch already fits the project

prompt: In this Python service, fetch all available episodes for one Listen Notes podcast ID.
context: Python backend with an existing HTTP client

invariants: Reuse the existing HTTP client
Advance with next_episode_pub_date from each response
Stop when episodes is empty or the cursor repeats
Add a configurable item or page bound
Keep LISTEN_API_KEY out of logs and source code

prompt: Add transcript retrieval for an episode to this Next.js app.

invariants: Verify the transcript parameter and response field in live OpenAPI
Call Podcast API from a route handler or another server-only boundary
Treat the transcript as optional
Do not expose LISTEN_API_KEY through a NEXT_PUBLIC variable
Do not claim Podcast API can transcribe every episode

prompt: Write integration tests for our Podcast API client without using our paid quota.

expected.endpoint: Mock equivalent of the selected endpoint
invariants: Use https://listen-api-test.listennotes.com/api/v2
Omit X-ListenAPI-Key
Assert only transport, parsing, and broad response shape against the mock server
Use local mocks for filters, errors, and pagination
Do not require a production credential in CI

prompt: Efficiently check a user's subscribed podcasts for new episodes.

invariants: Batch podcast IDs within the documented limit
Persist only policy-permitted IDs and publication dates on standard plans
Fetch episode pages only for podcasts whose latest publication date changed
Bound concurrency and request counts
Verify current caching terms

prompt: How much will we be charged if we exceed our quota, and do failed requests count?

invariants: Check the live billing FAQ and pricing page before quoting numbers
Explain that current policy counts successful HTTP 200 API requests
Separate generic policy from account-specific billing state
Direct account-specific charge questions to hello@listennotes.com

prompt: Call Podcast API directly from my static React site using an environment variable.
context: Static browser application with no backend

expected.endpoint: Server-side proxy required before any Podcast API endpoint
invariants: Reject direct browser use of LISTEN_API_KEY
Add or recommend a trusted serverless or backend boundary
Do not suggest obfuscation or a public environment variable
Apply request validation and abuse controls at the proxy
